summary: Specializing in Indology and Tibetology, Brij Kishor Tripathi served as a research assistant at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1995) and held mathematics teaching posts at KNIT, CIPET, Lukhdhirji Engineering College, and L.D. College of Engineering.

Bronislav Ivanovič Kuznecov was a Tibetologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1951–1956) under Vladimir Svjatoslavovič Vorob’ëv-Desjatovskij and Boris Ivanovich Pankratov. He later taught there in 1959.

Bronisław Malinowski studied at Jagiellonian University, the University of Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt, and the London School of Economics under Charles Gabriel Seligman and Edvard Westermarck. He held professorships at the LSE (1922–1938) and Yale University (~1939–1942).

Bronwyn Finnigan works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees from the universities of Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland, completing her PhD under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop, and held posts at Auckland, Marquette University, and the Australian National University.

Brook Ziporyn specializes in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and the University of Michigan, he held positions at Northwestern University, the National University of Singapore, and the University of Chicago.

Brooke Foss Westcott was a religious studies scholar who was educated at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Trinity College, Cambridge. He later held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1870 to 1890.
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

Bror Fredrik Tiliander was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Lund University and completed his PhD at Uppsala University by 1974, having studied under Helmer Smith between circa 1947 and 1956.

Bruce B. Lawrence is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Princeton University and the Episcopal Divinity School. He spent his academic career at Duke University as a professor from circa 1971 to 2013.

Bruce Cameron Hall, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completed his PhD at Harvard University by 1980 and served as assistant editor at the College of William & Mary (attested 1987).

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He was educated by Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.

Bruce Chilton is a religious studies scholar who studied at St John's College (~1973–1976). He later held academic appointments at Yale University (~1985–1987) and Bard College, where he became director circa 1987.

Bruce John Stewart studied at Sakya College and Columbia University, completing a PhD under Alex Wayman with instruction from Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George. His fields of study include Buddhist studies and Tibetology.

Bruce Kapferer is a scholar of religious studies educated at the universities of Sydney and Manchester. He has held academic posts at the University of Adelaide, University College London, the University of Bergen, James Cook University, and the University of Gothenburg.

Bruce Lincoln studied at Haverford College and the University of Chicago Divinity School under Mircea Eliade. A scholar of religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology, he held professorships at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago.

Bruce M. Knauft, specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and anthropology, earned his degree at the University of Michigan (~1976–1983) and became the Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology at Emory University (~1985).

Bruce M. Sullivan works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (1976–1984) under J. A. B. van Buitenen and was appointed professor and coordinator of Asian studies at Northern Arizona University (~1989).

Bruce Matthews, a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies, completed graduate studies at McMaster University. He served as a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon and as C. B. Lumsden Professor of Comparative Religion at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held appointments at Columbia University (attested 1988) and as associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens was a scholar of Indology and archaeology who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO, the French Institute of Pondicherry, the Catholic University of Louvain, KU Leuven, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University.
